thread.title: AMD, Netflix, Nvidia lead Silicon Valley stocks as Wall Street surges into New Year

author: SVBJ staff
title: AMD, Netflix, Nvidia lead Silicon Valley stocks as Wall Street surges into New Year

organizations.name: bloomberg silicon valley high tech index

text: By SVBJ staff Jan 2, 2018, 1:55pm PST Stocks got a healthy start in their first day of trading in 2018, with the Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Tech Index showing a 1.63 percent increase. Bloomberg's index — a roundup of 20 stocks of public companies either located in or doing significant business in Silicon Valley — revealed that all but one of the companies it tracks had a net positive day. Among Silicon Valley stocks on Bloomberg's index that made moves Tuesday: • Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) shares climbed 6.81 percent on Tuesday after rival Intel Corp. accidentally leaked details about a new chip that will use AMD graphics cards. Still, Sunnyvale-based AMD was the poorest performing stock in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index in 2017, Bloomberg reported , a stark reversal to 2016, when it was the top tech stock. • Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) shares gained 2.81 percent on Tuesday, brushing off concerns that the Menlo Park-based social media will face greater scrutiny and regulatory pressure in 2018. • Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) gained 1.79 percent after Piper Jaffray analyst reiterated his bullish outlook, saying he expects the Cupertino company's shares to continue their "super-long cycle” of price gains this year. Several Silicon Valley companies not on Bloomberg's list also saw big gains. Among them: • Shares of Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) jumped 4.75 percent after Citi analysts predicted there’s a 40 percent chance that cash-flush Apple buys the Los Gatos streaming video service. Another analyst upgraded his outlook on Netflix, saying the company “is miles ahead in terms of programming hours, original content quality and time spent, and we don't expect this to change.” • Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA) , an AMD and Intel rival , climbed 3.02 percent amid continued bullishness from analysts and investors. The Santa Clara-based chipmaker gained 82 percent last year, making it one of the best-performing tech stocks of 2017 . Nationally, the S&P 500 gained 0.8 percent to an intraday record, CNBC reported, while the Nasdaq surged 1.5 percent to a record high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 94 points, buoyed by Walt Disney Co. shares. Overall, the energy sector led the way, according to Bloomberg’s stock indices, climbing 1.78 percent on Tuesday. The consumer discretionary, materials, information technology and health care industries all outperformed the market, while the financials, consumer staples, real estate and utilities sectors fell.
